narratives.Overview:
The public `deftai/directive-training` course still teaches `@deftai/directive` **0.112.0** on every learner surface. The destination is the **latest published release** — npm `latest` is **0.119.2** as of 2026-09-17. A consumer `directive update` from the live CLI is not a safe first step: it would mix generations.

**Recut 2026-09-17 against `origin/master` `dc20d5e`.** This body supersedes the pre-#5 framing. Two things changed after it was filed:

1. PR #5 (`chore(deft): upgrade Directive to 0.119.1`) already landed the **authoring-pin tranche** on `master`. Root pin, `.deft/GENERATION.json`, managed `AGENTS.md`, `xbrief/.deft-version`, and the four host hook configs moved; every learner surface stayed at 0.112.0. The remaining contract is **collapse of that dual pin**, not a first bump.
2. npm `latest` moved from 0.119.1 to **0.119.2**. This issue targets whatever release is `latest` when the branch opens, bound by identity — not a version frozen into this body.

## Target release identity

Bind the release before any edit. Verified 2026-09-17:

| Surface | Value |
| --- | --- |
| npm `latest` (`@deftai/directive`) | `0.119.2` |
| integrity | `sha512-Ff7kcMu7n1FqslbB0TWW5lC4IebIVNUrJW8SyOeo8nA22xL/xwSh/BcisNbVaPiQRU14m6XVyCkWmEJI7XLvTg==` |
| annotated tag (`deftai/directive`) | `v0.119.2` → tag object `69b7e7c2ece41d5f330545c65ebf74a696706f41` |
| peeled commit / npm `gitHead` | `9038503ffac65e6d48e5ba34758c4e8e7077aba3` |
| live authoring CLI on this host | `@deftai/directive-core@0.119.2` |

**Binding rule.** If npm `latest` has moved again when work starts, re-resolve, record the new identity in this issue and in `SOURCE-BASELINE.md`, and implement that version. Do not carry two target versions at once: every probe, pin, and learner claim in the resulting PR names the same release.

**Freeze point.** The bind happens once, at branch open, and the first commit on the branch records the resolved identity in `SOURCE-BASELINE.md`. A release published after that commit is a follow-on issue, not a re-bind — the only exception being a release that invalidates a taught surface already probed on this branch, which is a re-bind with the probe campaign restarted and that fact recorded. Without this, "do not implement a superseded version" stays re-evaluable at review time and the probe campaign can never terminate.

Because acceptance can name no version literal (see finding 5: the verifiers derive theirs from the declared baseline), every literal in the PR is checked only against other literals in the same PR. The integrity hash, annotated tag, and peeled commit recorded in `SOURCE-BASELINE.md` are therefore the reviewer's only external anchor. That record is load-bearing; nothing checks it mechanically.

`@deftai/directive` declares caret ranges on core/content, core carets types/content, and this repository intentionally has no lockfile. The fixtures' exact four-package overrides are doing real reproducibility work, so every probe record must carry all four resolved versions (`@deftai/directive`, `-core`, `-content`, `-types`), run through the fixture-local launcher, and record `.deft/GENERATION.json` after `init`/`update`.

`references/SOURCE-BASELINE.md` — the repository's own evidence-precedence root — still asserts `package.json` has exact dev dependency `@deftai/directive: 0.112.0`, which is false at this SHA.

## Accepted design-critique findings

Round 3 closed `design-critique: synthesis accepted` (empty disagreement set), bound to successor lean `5714262466`, relief of Stop 1 `pain: P1` independently confirmed by pain-audit `5714338572`, verified-claims table `5714349814`. Findings 1-10 are folded into this body and re-measured at `dc20d5e` with the destination retargeted from 0.119.1 to npm `latest` (0.119.2).

That recut was then pain-audited on 2026-09-17 against `dc20d5e`, which returned `relieves: P1` — **no, not as written**, on four blocking grounds: the fixture launchers (finding 11), the `SOURCE-NOTES.md` current claim (finding 12), finding 5 naming three of ten assertion sites, and the binding rule's missing freeze point. All four are enumeration and freeze-point gaps rather than design disagreements; each is corrected above and none reopens the bind. That audit has not been posted to this thread.

### 1. The original starting state no longer exists — resolved by this recut

The pre-#5 facts table (teaching pin 0.112.0, GENERATION 0.117.0, `.deft/core/` absent, AGENTS rewrite reverted) was false at its own dispatch SHA and remains false at `dc20d5e`. An implementer reading it would re-bump surfaces that already moved and read the merged managed-section refresh as a default-branch defect, whose cheap "fix" is reverting PR #5. Amended above; PR #5 is named as tranche 0.

### 2. `Until this lands` is dropped; one policy, stated

The old paragraph forbade keeping an `agents:refresh` rewrite of tracked `AGENTS.md` on the default branch. `66f0712` did exactly that, with `change_class: none`, rewriting `AGENTS.md`, `.deft/GENERATION.json`, `package.json`, `xbrief/.deft-version`, `xbrief/PROJECT-DEFINITION.xbrief.json`, `.claude/settings.json`, `.codex/hooks.json`, `.cursor/hooks.json`, and `.grok/hooks/deft.json`. Two live records asserted incompatible policies, leaving "mixed generation" with no agreed referent.

**Policy for this issue:** the machine-managed framework layer may lead; the learner pin follows, and this issue is what makes it follow. `AGENTS.md` and the four host hook configs are named in this change's declared file scope, so any mid-branch re-stamp arrives as a reviewed diff rather than a refresh artifact. The old paragraph is deleted, not softened.

### 3. The validation baseline is red before any upgrade work — scoped dependency

`npm run check:module-11` fails at `dc20d5e` (re-run 2026-09-17): `missing heading: Current scope — Module 11 and capstone (2026-09-10)`. `scripts/verify-module-11.mjs:389` requires that heading; `COST-ESTIMATE.md` carries `Prior decision` / `Decision point` instead. Nine of the ten `check:*` content commands pass.

Without a green before-state, no regression can be attributed to the upgrade, and the acceptance line "focused checks pass" pressures the worker into editing an unrelated estimate or weakening a verifier to clear inherited red. **Disposition:** land the Module 11 / COST-ESTIMATE heading correction first and start from a green tree, or carry it explicitly as a scoped dependency of this change with its own rationale and regression proof. Do not let it be cleared silently inside the upgrade diff.

### 4. Version occurrences are three classes, not one

A bounded grep finds ~80 candidate paths outside completed/cancelled scopes, history, approved-scope records, `CHANGELOG.md`, and `COST-ESTIMATE.md` — and they are not one semantic class. `SOURCE-NOTES.md` deliberately holds a `Historical 0.112.0 learner-baseline version and provenance probes` section. Literal replacement would relabel old observations as the new version; a prose-only pass leaves an executable fixture or verifier stale while the aggregate gate still passes, exactly as the current tree demonstrates.

`SOURCE-NOTES.md` belongs to **both** classes and must be split, not filed wholesale under preserve: its `## Verification context` block is a current claim (see finding 12), everything from `## Historical 0.112.0 learner-baseline version and provenance probes` down is history.

**Policy:** classify every occurrence as `re-probe and replace`, `preserve as labeled historical evidence`, or `remove as superseded`, and say which in the PR.

### 5. The coupling gate was retargeted, not tripped — at least one criterion must fail today

`6a2c498` retargeted the root-pin assertion from `0.112.0` to `0.119.1`. `git grep -n '0\.119\.1' dc20d5e -- 'scripts/verify-*'` shows **ten** production sites carrying that assertion, not three:

`verify-capstone.mjs:553`, `verify-cold-start-readme.mjs:21`, `verify-module-6.mjs:200`, `verify-module-7.mjs:180`, `verify-module-8.mjs:168`, `verify-module-9.mjs:193`, `verify-module-10.mjs:202`, `verify-module-11.mjs:492`, `verify-modules-2-3.mjs:431`, `verify-modules-4-5.mjs:224` — plus `verify-capstone.test.mjs`, `verify-module-6.test.mjs`, `verify-module-11.test.mjs`, and `verify-modules-4-5.test.mjs`, which encode both pins.

Nine of the ten also keep 0.112.0 assertions on taught content, so they now certify the split. The old acceptance criterion "focused checks pass" is satisfied on the exact state this issue exists to end.

`verify-cold-start-readme.mjs` is the exception: it contains no 0.112.0 taught-baseline assertion at all, so it has nothing local to derive from. Couple it to `README.md:29` ("Note the current teaching baseline: `@deftai/directive` 0.112.0"), which no verifier currently asserts.

**Disposition:** one shared derived-literal helper, read by all ten sites, taking its expected value from the declared teaching baseline — not three independent rewrites, and not a new `verify-baseline-pin.mjs` or version-drift framework. Retargeting only three leaves seven hand-edited hardcoded literals, which is the same drift channel this finding exists to close.

### 6. Named gates run nowhere in CI

No workflow invokes any `check:` script. `task deft:check` appears once outside the deposit, as a checkbox in `.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md`; root `Taskfile.yml` includes `./.deft/core/Taskfile.yml` with `optional: true`, and `.deft/core/` is gitignored, so `deft:check` does not exist on a CI checkout. `deft-core-guard.yml` runs on every PR but its `.deft/core/**` arm is permanently inert for the same reason. `modules-2-3-platform-validation.yml` is path-filtered to five module-02 files, so it did not run on PR #5 even though PR #5 changed the root pin. Edits to `curriculum/`, `solutions/`, `assessments/`, and `references/SOURCE-BASELINE.md` trigger no workflow at all.

**Disposition:** the PR names who runs the `check:*` set and where that evidence is recorded, or wires them in. Acceptance cannot cite them as gates while nothing runs them.

### 7. Lab 2's init disagreement has a 0.119.1 answer; the open probe is ownership

A non-mutating `directive init --headless --repo-root .` on the **0.119.1** CLI emitted `package.json` as `{"private": true, "devDependencies": {"@deftai/directive": "0.119.1"}}` (422 files, 7 non-deposit), which would resolve Lab 2's recorded "init created no package pin" disagreement (`SOURCE-NOTES.md:899`).

Treat that as a **0.119.1 observation, unconfirmed on the bound release** — not as resolved. Tier 1 of `SOURCE-BASELINE.md`'s evidence-precedence order is the *pin-matched* CLI, and a 0.119.1 CLI is not pin-matched to 0.119.2. No 0.119.1 probe may be cited in `SOURCE-BASELINE.md` or in any lab without a bound-release re-run; `#4562` (update staged-index refresh) in particular touches the file-writing path.

The consequence is the real open question: `modules-2-3-platform-validation.yml` copies `labs/fixtures/02-disposable-initialization/package.json` into the lab root **before** running `directive init --yes --repo-root .`. Both the fixture and init now own that file. Whether init overwrites, merges, or leaves the learner's pin is behavior Lab 2 teaches and no record covers. The first probe on the new pin is an **unpinned disposable init in a no-remote temp repo**; keep, drop, or recast the pre-seeded pin only from that result. Bumping the fixture string while keeping "copy pin, then init" would teach a 0.112.0 workaround as current doctrine.

### 8. Alignment is the exit, not a pre-edit gate

`maintainers/CURRICULUM-MAINTENANCE.md` release revalidation step 4 says to stop the content change if project pin, installed engine, tag, and commit SHA cannot be aligned. Run as a pre-edit gate on today's dual-pin tree, it halts this cutover and preserves the mixed state. Treat this as a baseline cutover of the same shape as completed `training.directive-baseline-0.112.0`: alignment is the exit condition of this PR. Do not add a new procedure document.

### 9. Current-claim completeness (parent take on pain-audit heading 3)

`references/GLOSSARY.md`, `references/QUICK-REFERENCE.md`, `maintainers/CURRICULUM-MAINTENANCE.md`, `maintainers/WINDOWS-REVALIDATION.md`, and `scripts/restore-validation-deposit.mjs` are current claims at 0.112.0 that the accepted lean did not name. Leaving them out does not reopen P1, but this recut finishes current-claim collapse in one pass, so they are in the remaining contract. Note that `restore-validation-deposit.mjs` cannot run against this clone today (it refuses unless root pin and GENERATION are 0.112.0) and must be retargeted with the rest.

### 10. Anchors that hold

- `verify:vbrief-conformance` is still registered on 0.119.x.
- The three recorded `--help` defects (`toolchain:check`, `verify:ac`, `check` each exit 2 with `unrecognized argument: --help`) survived the 0.119.1 bump, and `modules-2-3-platform-validation.yml` still asserts that exit. This is a 0.119.1 observation, unconfirmed on the bound release; re-probe before resolving "keep, drop, or recast". The same demotion applies to every 0.119.1 record carried forward in this body.
- Platform-label restraint already lives in PROJECT-DEFINITION `SupportedEnvironments`. No new mechanism.
- PR #5 also enabled `valueFeedback` and `productSignal` on `xbrief/PROJECT-DEFINITION.xbrief.json`. Keep those flags out of this bump.

### 11. The executable fixture launchers are the decisive omission

`class: blocks-the-design` — from the 2026-09-17 pain audit of this recut.

"Fixture manifests" means the six `package.json` files, and nothing else. Beside them sit five launchers that are not manifests and were not named:

- `labs/fixtures/07-scope-lifecycle/lifecycle-lab.mjs:23` — `const exactVersion = "0.112.0";`
- `labs/fixtures/09-implementation-golden-path/implementation-lab.mjs:24` — same
- `labs/fixtures/10-testing-gates-and-evidence/gates-lab.mjs:24` — same
- `labs/fixtures/capstone-end-to-end/capstone-lab.mjs:26` — same
- `labs/fixtures/05-projection-drift-recovery/projection-lab.mjs:119-126` — inline literals and `return "0.112.0"`

They are fail-closed guards, not decorative strings: `assert.equal(manifest.devDependencies?.["@deftai/directive"], exactVersion, "exact 0.112.0 pin required")`, the matching `overrides` asserts, `name + " must resolve to 0.112.0"`, and `assert.match(read(".deft/core/VERSION"), /(?:ref|tag): 'v0\.112\.0'/, "Stop: Directive deposit must be 0.112.0.")`. `lifecycle-lab.mjs:259` also pins fixture digests.

**Failure mode.** Collapse the six manifests and the prose, ship, and a learner on Lab 7/9/10/capstone hits `exact 0.112.0 pin required` — or after `init`/`update`, `Stop: Directive deposit must be 0.112.0.` The labs do not teach a wrong surface; they refuse to start. P1's mixed generation moves out of prose and into the executables, and the aggregate `check:*` set still goes green because no `check:*` script reads these files.

The same shape, one tier weaker, covers seven maintainer test files that no `check:*` runs: `scripts/{capstone,gates,implementation,lifecycle,projection}-lab.test.mjs`, `linked-path-safety.test.mjs`, `restore-validation-deposit.test.mjs`. Several encode negative-mutation constants that flip `0.112.0` → `0.113.0` to prove drift is caught; once the baseline moves past 0.113.0 those mutate to a version *older* than the pin and stop testing drift in the intended direction.

**Disposition:** in-scope item 2 names `labs/**` (including `labs/README.md` and `labs/fixtures/**`) and `scripts/*.test.mjs`, and the quality gate adds `npm run test:*`. The `0.113.0` mutation constants need a bound-release-relative successor.

### 12. `SOURCE-NOTES.md` carries a false current pin claim

`class: blocks-the-design` — from the 2026-09-17 pain audit.

`references/SOURCE-NOTES.md:12`, under the header `Current-baseline verification date: 2026-09-12`:

> - Project direct pin: `@deftai/directive` 0.112.0 in `devDependencies`.

False at `dc20d5e`, where root is `0.119.1` — the identical defect this body already calls out in `SOURCE-BASELINE.md`. Its sibling bullets were deliberately relabeled (`Historical learner-baseline executable context…`, `…installed package graph…`, `…deposit proof…`); this one was missed. Lines 22-26 of the same section are stale in the other direction ("deposit 0.117.0", superseded by PR #5).

**Failure mode.** An implementer applying the occurrence policy files the whole file under preserve-as-history and touches nothing. Tier 3 of `SOURCE-BASELINE.md`'s evidence-precedence order then points at a document whose current-context header asserts the project pin is 0.112.0 while every other surface names the bound release — P1 in miniature, surviving the change meant to end it.

**Disposition:** split the file per finding 4. Retarget or relabel the `## Verification context` block; preserve everything below the historical header.

### 13. `ROADMAP.md` is a stale projection with no bucket

`class: sharpens-framing` — from the 2026-09-17 pain audit.

`ROADMAP.md:271`, under `## Acceptance` of "Complete native Windows learner paths for Labs 7, 9, and 10 (#78)": "Each helper installs and verifies the exact CLI/core/content/types 0.112.0 graph on Windows." That section renders in the **forward** block, but `xbrief/pending/` holds only `.gitkeep` and all five rendered forward sections have their xBRIEFs in `xbrief/completed/`. The projection is stale against its own declared source of truth.

The file is `AUTO-GENERATED by task roadmap:render — DO NOT EDIT MANUALLY`, and per finding 6 that task does not exist on any checkout. So it is not in the remaining contract, not in Out of scope, and not in the occurrence policy's exclusion list.

**Failure mode.** After the collapse the roadmap still states, as an open acceptance criterion, that Windows helpers verify the exact 0.112.0 graph. A course that teaches source-versus-projection in Module 5 ships a stale projection of a retired pin.

**Disposition:** give it an explicit line — regenerate once `.deft/core/` is present and record that the render produced the diff, or declare it out of scope as a stale projection with its own issue. Do not leave it unclassified. (`ROADMAP.md:313`, the completed-scope index entry, is correctly history.)

## Why not just run `directive update`

Ordinary consumer upgrade (`npm i -g @deftai/directive@latest` then `directive update`) refreshes the untracked `.deft/core/` payload and tracked installer-managed files such as `AGENTS.md`. That is the authoring half, and it has already happened once at 0.119.1.

This repository's product is the **pinned teaching baseline**. Labs, solutions, and focused checks fail closed on exact literals. Running `update` again on the authoring pin does nothing for the learner surfaces and re-stamps the instruction boundary a second time. A training upgrade PR is pin + curriculum + fixtures + baseline evidence, not a framework-payload commit. `.deft/core/` stays untracked.

## In scope (remaining contract)

1. Bind the latest release identity (npm graph with all four resolved versions, integrity, annotated tag, peeled commit, help/command probes) and record it in `SOURCE-BASELINE.md`.
2. Collapse the learner pin to that release:
   - `labs/**` — the six fixture manifests **and** the five fixture launchers (`labs/fixtures/*/*.mjs`, finding 11), the six lab documents, and `labs/README.md` (whose readiness table ties every platform label to 0.112.0 evidence)
   - `curriculum/` (13 files), `solutions/` (13 files), `assessments/capstone-end-to-end.md`
   - `README.md` — the "Start here" teaching-baseline line at `:29` and the Module 2 claim at `:64`
   - `references/SOURCE-BASELINE.md`, `references/GLOSSARY.md`, `references/QUICK-REFERENCE.md`, and the `## Verification context` block of `references/SOURCE-NOTES.md` (finding 12)
   - `maintainers/CURRICULUM-MAINTENANCE.md`, `maintainers/WINDOWS-REVALIDATION.md`, `scripts/restore-validation-deposit.mjs`
   - `.github/workflows/modules-2-3-platform-validation.yml`
   - the verifier literals that lock those claims: the ten root-pin sites in `scripts/verify-*.mjs` (finding 5), their `scripts/verify-*.test.mjs` companions, and `scripts/*-lab.test.mjs` (finding 11)
   - `ROADMAP.md` per finding 13
   Move the authoring surfaces (`package.json`, `.deft/GENERATION.json`, `AGENTS.md`, `xbrief/.deft-version`, host hooks) from 0.119.1 to the same release in the same PR.
3. Re-run taught command surfaces in disposable no-remote labs (`init`, `update`, `doctor`, `toolchain:check`, scope lifecycle, session ritual, `verify:story-ready`, `xbrief:preflight`, `verify:ac`, `verify:forward-coverage`, `check`). Record `--help` rejections instead of inventing syntax. Start with the unpinned disposable `init` probe from finding 7.
4. Reconcile current learner and maintainer docs with observed behavior on the bound release; leave historical 0.112.0 records in place, labeled as history.
5. Apply the three-way occurrence policy (finding 4) and derive the verifier literal from the declared baseline (finding 5).
6. Keep platform labels evidence-bounded. Do not promote Linux/Windows to revalidated without a native matrix (or a walkthrough that records an actual native run, environment, command, exit, and artifact) on the new pin.

## Out of scope

- Recutting 3Ci vs DeftAI identity, visibility, or `ProjectRules` — that is #2.
- Adding an MIT license — that is #1.
- Historical completed xBRIEFs, archived 0.111.0/0.112.0 evidence, and byte-for-byte old delivery records.
- Inventing a large version-drift framework. A repeatable maintainer workflow already lives as proposed scope `xbrief/proposed/2026-09-05-version-drift-and-maintenance-process.xbrief.json`; do not block this baseline bump on that process work.
- Committing `.deft/core/`.
- Push, PR, merge, or publication without a later explicit instruction.
- Learner exercises inside this working tree.

## Teaching-relevant deltas to re-probe (0.113.0 → bound release)

Investigation inputs, not a rewrite list. Confirm against the pin-matched CLI before changing lessons:

- Init pin behavior (`#4429`) vs Lab 2's 0.112.0 "no package pin" disagreement — see finding 7; the fixture-vs-init ownership question is the live one
- Doctor layout split (`#4162`) and dirty-tree `update` refuse (`#4158`)
- Session ritual default 8 hours (`#4406`); requirements posture (`#4444`) is not beginner-path
- Merge chokepoint prefers `deft check` (`#4379`)
- New optional gates (`verify:intent-constraint`, `verify:observable-scope`, `verify:evaluator-surface`, `verify:consumer-test-lane`) stay out of the beginner path unless a module already teaches the surrounding contract
- Known `--help` defects (`toolchain:check`, `verify:ac`, `check`) — keep, drop, or recast from live exits
- **0.119.1 → 0.119.2 (32 commits, 89 files), diffed 2026-09-17 — all on the beginner path:**
  - `update` names staged index files on clean-tree refresh (`#4562`) — Lab 5 exercises `update`
  - `scope complete` refuses when acceptance clauses lack evidence (`#4385`) — Modules 7 and 11
  - honest occupancy mandate for CLI `complete` and `check` (`#4625`)
  - drop-flag suffix on `verify:session-ritual --session-id` (`#4641`) — Module 8's session ritual

  - maintainer `.gitignore` un-ignores provenance under `.deft/approved-scope` and `.deft/intent-constraint` (explicitly *not* the consumer `CANONICAL_GITIGNORE_BASELINE`)
- If the bind lands past 0.119.2, this delta is not yet enumerated for that window — diff it before probing

## Acceptance

- Every maintained package and executable surface — authoring **and** learner — pins `@deftai/directive` at the single bound release exactly, with matching core/content/types where the course requires that graph. No file declares a different version except as labeled history.
- The five fixture launchers and the seven lab/unit test files start clean on the bound release: `npm run test:*` is green, not just `check:*`.
- **The derived-literal assertion fails when run against `dc20d5e` content and passes only after the collapse.** All ten root-pin sites read one shared helper that takes its expected value from the declared teaching baseline, so root pin and curriculum declaration cannot disagree silently. The inherited `check:module-11` heading failure does **not** satisfy this criterion — it is red for an unrelated reason and would otherwise let a heading edit in `COST-ESTIMATE.md` stand in for the coupling.
- Current learner and maintainer references describe only behavior observed or sourced from the bound release; still-present defects stay explicit.
- `SOURCE-BASELINE.md` records the bound release identity (four resolved versions, integrity, tag, peeled commit), probe surfaces, disagreements, and verification date.
- Historical 0.112.0 delivery records remain unchanged and are labeled as history.
- The inherited `check:module-11` failure is disposed per finding 3 — fixed ahead of this change or carried as a named scoped dependency with regression proof — and the full `check:*` set is green at the end, with the runner and evidence location named per finding 6.
- `AGENTS.md` and the four host hook configs are in the declared file scope, and any re-stamp during the branch appears as a reviewed diff.
- Linux/Windows learner-ready labels are not promoted without native evidence on the new pin.
